newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index up 1.3pct despite Iraq concern.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index up 1.3pct despite Iraq concern.

text.p: Kuwait's share index rose 1.36 percent in the week ending Wednesday despite warning by the prime minister about former occupier Iraq remaining a "threat".
The index rose 25.8 points to 1,913.2 points from 1,887.4 last week, the Kuwait Stock Exchange said in a statement on Thursday. Gainers led losers 19-11, while 20 were non-movers.
Total traded shares value rose to 136.7 million dinars ($455.6 million) from 129 million the previous week. Volume rose to 496.6 million shares from 333.3 million.
"The market was not affected by the speech," said dealer Mohammad al-Duhaishi referring to Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah's address to parliament on Tuesday.
Sheikh Saad said Iraq remained a threat to Kuwait's security and asked MPs to focus attention on security-related matters.
The exchange operates for 2-1/2 hours five days a week.
But trade levels were still below those reached in October.
"Historically, the market slows down in December..." before year-end, said Nasser Bou-Resli, a portfolio manager at Coast Development.
Also, "the privatisation of the Securities Group absorbed much of the liquidity in the market," added another dealer.
The state sold 220 million shares of its stake in the Securties Group through public subscription earlier this month.
Speculation on the impact of a dispute over the chairmanship of parliament also slowed trade at the exchange, dealers said.
The row was triggered by former finance minister MP Jassem al-Kharafi, who says the October 20 re-election of opposition veteran Ahmad al-Saadoun as speaker was unconstitutional.
Parliament decided last week to refer the dispute to the constitutional court.
By sector, banks led trading by value, with 33.6 million dinars, followed by investment firms with 32.5 million and property firms with 27.0 million.
Commercial Bank, Gulf Bank, Investment Projects, Coast Development, The International Investor and United Realty were among the most traded shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
Kuwait is considering opening trade for foreign investors.
